- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing the true mean-reversion trend.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — overreacting to volatility.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in high-variance periods (e.g., 2024-05–06), underestimating downward corrections.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 3–7 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in medium-term (15–30 day) horizons — overestimates persistence of trends.
- In low-variance periods, model underestimates price stability and fails to adjust for minor corrections.
- Forecasts show diminishing accuracy as horizon extends beyond 20 days — model loses sensitivity to short-term volatility.
